Action Plan:
1. Arrange urgent face-to-face review for full abdominal and pelvic examination (patient to phone support line and book same-day/next-day appointment).
2. Patient to perform a urine pregnancy test today; if positive, contact the service immediately for same-day assessment (rule out possible early/ectopic pregnancy).
3. Safety-net advice given: attend ED or call service sooner if pain escalates, heavy vaginal bleeding, vomiting preventing oral intake, dizziness/syncope, or new concerning symptoms.
4. Documented allergy to amoxicillin noted; avoid prescribing amoxicillin-containing antibiotics.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• 23-year-old female presents with constant lower-midline abdominal pain, onset “a few days ago,” progressively worsening, current intensity ~8/10.  
• Associated symptoms: light pink vaginal bleeding outside normal menses; nausea without vomiting; constipation for one week (resolved); no diarrhea; no fever, dyspnea, shoulder pain, syncope, urinary pain, or dysuria.  
• Last menstrual period: ~2–3 weeks ago, described as normal.  
• Sexual activity: regular; last intercourse 4 days ago; uses Implanon contraceptive implant (inserted ~1 year ago).  
• Pregnancy test performed ~1 month ago (negative); none since onset of pain.  
• Past medical history: none reported.  
• Surgical history: none.  
• Allergies: amoxicillin (reaction type not specified).  
• Medications: Implanon contraceptive implant (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Social: Primary school teacher; lives with husband and husband’s family; denies smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs; no recent travel (last travel ~1 year ago).

Objective:
• Remote video consultation – no physical examination performed.  
• No vitals available.  
• No investigations performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain / pelvic pain  
   - Assessment: Pelvic pain, possible early intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy, pelvic inflammatory disease, gastrointestinal etiology.  
   - Differential diagnosis: ectopic pregnancy, early pregnancy, PID, ovarian cyst/torsion, UTI, constipation-related pain, dysmenorrhea.  
   - Investigations planned: Urine pregnancy test today; in-person abdominal & pelvic examination; consider urine dipstick, pelvic ultrasound, CBC, inflammatory markers once examined.  
   - Treatment planned: Analgesia if required (not prescribed remotely); safety-net advice; avoid amoxicillin if antibiotics later needed.  
   - Referrals: Face-to-face GP review; possible same-day gynecology referral if pregnancy test positive or examination concerning.

2. Irregular/light vaginal bleeding  
   - Assessment: Intermenstrual bleeding—needs evaluation for hormonal breakthrough bleed vs pregnancy-related bleed vs infection.  
   - Investigations planned: Included above (pregnancy test, pelvic exam, possible swabs).  
   - Treatment planned: As per findings after examination.  
   - Referrals: As above.

3. Nausea ± previous constipation  
   - Assessment: Likely secondary to primary abdominal/pelvic pathology.  
   - Treatment planned: Encourage hydration; monitor; address underlying cause.  

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: no vitals, no detailed allergy reaction, no comprehensive medication list beyond implant, no analgesia documented.  
• No internal contradictions noted.  
• Transcript quality: generally clear; occasional inaudible words but clinical content preserved.
